errors.text: Identifies the CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy rather than the targeted Fe-Co-Ni-Ti-derived dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy.
Frames the target as finite-temperature magnetic moments and phase stability rather than improvement of coercivity beyond the approximately 100 Oe single-phase-fcc limit.
Replaces the relevant fcc/C14 Laves-phase coupling and domain-wall-pinning mechanism with longitudinal spin fluctuations in a single-phase paramagnetic alloy.

Misstates the orbital-moment challenge as primarily a deficiency of itinerant-magnetism theory; the target concerns how a small fcc orbital contribution can enhance coercivity when coupled to the C14 phase and spin-canted components.
The cited evidence supports longitudinal-spin-fluctuation calculations for CoCrFeMnNi but does not substantiate the asserted orbital-moment claims or the target coercivity mechanism.
